$description: Machine index of the ObserveOps design system — load FIRST.
$contract: ../AGENTS.md — the AI Operating Contract. READ BEFORE BUILDING: use only catalogued components, resolve every colour to a token, compose pages from recipes/layout, and STOP-and-ASK before using anything not in this DS. This index is step 1 of that contract.
$howToUse: 1. Find by need (family/category/selectHint/summary or scan variants).
3. Resolve --var in tokensUsed via tokens/variables.json (LESS @vars: tokens/structural.json).

5. To lay out a PAGE (not just a component): load `layout.spec` (layout/layouts.json) — shells (4 route + 2 content), screenRegions, contentLayouts (6), panels (10), pageTemplates (7, each → a recipe). Region→component blueprints are in `recipes` (recipes.json). `layout.grid` = the 12-col grid. `layout.coverage` (foundation/) = which product pages use each.

6. Styling a NEW element that isn't a catalogued component? DON'T hardcode colours — pick the token by PURPOSE in `tokens.purposeMap` (tokens/purpose-map.json): surface/text/border/brand/status/severity/shadow → token (+ light/dark), plus the structural spacing/sizing/radius/type scale.

tokens.$use: RESOLVE + EMIT runtime CSS vars: component tokensUsed -> tokens/variables.json (336 --vars, light/dark) + structural.json (LESS @vars: spacing/sizing/type) + kit-accents.json (@primary-color). This is the LIVE product token layer — use it.
tokens.$future: tokens/{primitive,semantic.light,semantic.dark,component}.json define a FUTURE portable DTCG system (mds-* names). It is NOT yet wired to components or the running product — do NOT emit mds-* tokens for live output. Use --vars (variables.json) today.

layout.$note: The structural layer — the 12-col grid (MRow/MCol) + app shell, layout shells, screen regions & panel behaviours (layout/layouts.json; Storybook: Foundations/Layout/*). foundation/*.md = a page-by-page PRODUCT coverage sweep per element (which pages/flows use each variant + findings + best practices).

components.summary: Primary action control. Triggers an operation or navigation.
components.selectHint: Navigates (route/URL/anchor)? -> link (FlotoLink), not a button.

components.summary: Single boolean toggle, usually with a label. Functional, fully-controlled.
components.selectHint: Mutually-exclusive (pick one)? -> MRadio.

components.summary: The product's chart & widget hover tooltips — a distinct family from MTooltip, owned by the chart layer (Highcharts TooltipBuilder, graph canvases, widget Vue components), not DS components. ~28 reference reproductions cover every mechanism.
components.selectHint: Hover detail on a CHART/graph/canvas mark? -> data-viz tooltip (owned by the chart layer, not MTooltip).

components.summary: The product's date/time selection family. The hero is TimeRangePicker (42×) — the observability time-range control (relative presets + absolute custom range). MDatePicker (10×, wraps a-date-picker) is the form date-time field, in practice ALWAYS used with show-time. MTimePicker wraps a-time-picker (12-hour) but is rarely used standalone. DateTimePopover is a lighter custom-range-only popover. TimeRangeSlider is a FUNCTIONAL, LINKABLE timeline scrubber — drive its window/band from a range picker via range-start/range-end.
components.selectHint: Pick a chart/dashboard/log TIME WINDOW → range (or range-presets); a date/time VALUE in a form → field-datetime/field-date/field-time; a draggable timeline SCRUBBER (optionally linked to a range picker) → slider.

components.summary: A thin rule that marks a semantic break — horizontal between stacked sections, vertical between inline items.
components.selectHint: Separate sections (horizontal) or inline items (vertical). If you only need space, use margin, not a divider.

components.summary: Slide-in side panel (from the right) for detail views, edit forms, and record-contextual content. The product's MOST-used overlay (FlotoDrawer 99x + FlotoDrawerForm 59x = 158x). Open via open prop or trigger slot.
components.selectHint: Short yes/no or destructive confirmation? -> FlotoConfirmModal, not a drawer.

components.summary: The product's custom select: popover-anchored, virtualized, searchable, single/multi-select, keyboard nav, optional inline-add. Not a native/Ant select.
components.selectHint: Free-form typed tags? -> LooseTags, not the picker.

components.summary: The product's filtering components, grouped by ARCHETYPE (not by the screen they sit in). Four distinct kinds: the Expression builder (nested AND/OR query builder), the Filter bar (inline chips), Quick filters (preset menu), and the Filter row (multi-selects + Reset/Apply). These are molecules; the Toolbars (organisms) compose them.
components.selectHint: Complex AND/OR conditions across multiple groups? -> Expression builder (FiltersContainer, 32×).

components.summary: The form field: label + validation + control + error/help. MValidationProvider (vee-validate) -> MFormItem. Most-used component (1783x). required is derived from rules.
components.selectHint: Building a form field (label + control + validation)? -> FlotoFormItem (always).

components.summary: Text input. A type-router (text/password/number/search/textarea/datetime). v-model is value+update. Almost always wrapped by FlotoFormItem for label+validation.
components.selectHint: Multi-line text? -> type=textarea (or FlotoFormItem type=textarea).

components.summary: Navigation control. Default renders a RouterLink (<a>); as-button renders an MButton that pushes the route on click. Only own prop is asButton; everything else passes through.
components.selectHint: Performs an action (save/delete/change state)? -> Button, not a link.

components.summary: Free-form tag input (type to create tags) with async suggestions. The Tag family's input member; home of the teal pills.
components.selectHint: Just displaying tags (label/count/status)? -> MTag/MStatusTag, not LooseTags.

components.summary: The MMenu primitive (a vertical list of selectable icon+label rows, with dividers and danger/positive colours) catalogued in its own right, plus its action-surface usage: the Context/Action menu (FlotoGridActions — a '...' trigger opening an MMenu of actions).
components.selectHint: A list of items to render inside something (nav, picker, dropdown)? -> Menu primitive.

components.summary: The DS modal dialog (obs-modal) — a centered dialog over a blurred backdrop (native <dialog>); title + close ✕, footer, and confirm/hide-footer/no-padding/scrollable/restrict-width variants.
components.selectHint: Yes/no or destructive confirmation? -> FlotoConfirmModal (variant=error for destructive).

components.summary: The product's wayfinding components, by archetype: Primary nav (left module sidebar), Side menu (searchable collapsible section menu), Steps (wizard/stepper), Breadcrumb (back + trail), Back button. Tabs are their own family (Molecules/Tabs).
components.selectHint: Switch between top-level product MODULES? -> Primary nav (left sidebar).

components.summary: Click-triggered floating panel anchored to a trigger, holding interactive content (action menus, pickers, mini-forms). Slots trigger/title/default each get {hide,show,toggle}. MPopper is the lower-level v-popover positioning primitive that powers FlotoDropdownPicker.
components.selectHint: Is the content a short non-interactive hint? -> Tooltip, not Popover.

components.summary: One-of-many selection control. Use MRadioGroup with :options + v-model; as-button renders a segmented control. Standalone MRadio is unused.
components.selectHint: Multi-select (pick any number)? -> Checkbox.

components.summary: A composite recurrence builder. A 'Scheduler Type' segmented control (MRadioGroup as-button: Once · Daily · Weekly · Monthly) swaps in a sub-form. Once/Daily = Start Date + Hours; Weekly adds Days (Mon-Sun); Monthly adds Months + Dates (1-31). Hours = the custom dropdown TimePicker (multi-select times); Days/Months/Dates = FlotoDropdownPicker multi-selects; Start Date = MDatePicker (date-only, min-date today). Used for backups, network discovery, compliance audits, monitor (re)discovery, reports, runbooks.
components.selectHint: Need a RECURRING schedule (run X every day/week/month)? -> ScheduleInput.

components.summary: Kit's raw Ant a-select wrapper. LOW-USE (2x, both mode=tags) — the product's select is FlotoDropdownPicker (510x). Modes default/multiple/tags; v-model value/change.
components.selectHint: Need the product's standard select (single/multi/search/virtualized/custom trigger)? -> FlotoDropdownPicker (the norm, 510x).

components.summary: The severity INDICATOR — a coloured dot (+ optional label + tooltip) for a severity LEVEL (down / critical / major / warning / clear / up / maintenance / unreachable / unknown / …). Distinct from MStatusTag, which maps status STRINGS to tag-* pills. Used 80×. Renders --severity-<level>; can take `severity` directly or resolve it live from a monitor (objectId / instance / counter) via DB workers.
components.selectHint: Showing a monitor/alert SEVERITY level (critical/major/warning/clear/up/down/…)? -> Severity (dot).

components.summary: A responsive severity LEGEND — the row of coloured dots + labels (Down / Critical / Major / Warning / Clear / Unreachable …) under a table, map or chart. Composes obs-severity for every entry. When the container is too narrow, trailing entries COLLAPSE into a '+N' pill with their dots piled up (avatar-style) and a hover popover reveals them; with room, every entry shows in full.
related: table (the legend goes in its footer slot)
pagination (hosts the legend in its centered slot)

components.summary: Instant on/off toggle for a setting that applies immediately. Controlled.
components.selectHint: Mutually-exclusive options? -> MRadio.

components.summary: The DS data table (obs-table) — sortable columns, selection, rich cells (severity/status/type), row actions, pagination. The product Kendo Grid/VirtualTable, everywhere.
components.selectHint: Need to fetch + paginate a list with CRUD? -> FlotoPaginatedCrud (wraps MGrid; handles fetch/paging/search/filters).

components.summary: The DS pagination footer as a standalone element — reusable under ANY paged view (table, card grid, list). Seek controls (first/prev · numbered SQUARES · next/last, Material-Symbols skip glyphs) + a page-size select + a 'start - end of N items' range, with a CENTERED slot for extra footer content (e.g. a severity legend).
related: select (the page-size control is a native styled select)

components.summary: In-page tabbed navigation that switches between sibling views of one context. MTab wraps Ant a-tabs; panes are MTabPane. The product uses ONLY line-style, top-positioned, default-size tabs — Ant's card/editable-card/vertical/size/tabBarExtraContent features are available but unused in-product. Active tab = --primary (text + underline + ink bar); inactive = --tabs-text-color; bar bottom border = --border-color. Real variants are class-based.
components.selectHint: Switching between sibling VIEWS of one context (not navigating to other pages)? -> Tabs. (For page nav use the router/menu.)

components.summary: A wizard/stepper — a numbered progress track through the ordered stages of a multi-step flow, showing which steps are done, which is current, and which remain.
components.selectHint: Use for a linear multi-step flow (a create/import wizard, a guided form). NOT for switching between peer sections of one page (that is obs-tabs), and NOT for navigating between pages (obs-breadcrumbs / obs-sidebar).

components.summary: Compact label for categorization or removable selections. Used as a plain tag; color variants are broken.
components.selectHint: User types/adds tags? -> LooseTags (input), not Tag.

components.summary: Read-only tag overflow display: up to maxLength neutral chips, else a count chip + hover popover. UNUSED in product (0 usages) — prefer SelectedItemPills.
components.selectHint: Tag overflow display (show some, +N rest)? -> SelectedItemPills (or LooseTags :disabled), NOT TagsList.

components.summary: The product's toolbar compositions, as variants of one family. A toolbar is an organism that arranges molecules/atoms (title, search, filters, actions). Variants: Page header, Widget header, Bulk action bar, Grid toolbar, Column chooser.
components.selectHint: Top of a list/detail page (title + actions)? -> Page header.

components.summary: Transient hover/focus label anchored to a trigger. The kit MTooltip is excluded and this Floto override ships instead, rendering through VTippy (not a-tooltip). trigger slot = anchor, default slot = content. Non-interactive — for interactive panels use Popover.
components.selectHint: Is the content interactive (buttons, inputs, links)? -> use Popover, NOT a tooltip.

components.summary: The product's charts, stat tiles, topology graph and dashboard grid — a decision GUIDE, not a web component. Charts are Highcharts v10, topology is Cytoscape, the dashboard grid is vue-grid-layout: all app-rendered and licensed/heavy, so the DS does not ship an obs-* for them. Use this to pick the RIGHT visualisation type and colour/token it on-brand, then render it with the product's Chart/Graph/Widgets component (in-repo) or STOP-and-ASK (standalone).
components.selectHint: Any CHART / graph / gauge / KPI tile / heatmap / topology map / dashboard grid: pick the type via decisionFlow, colour from chart-palette, then render with the product's Chart/Graph/Widgets component. No obs-* — standalone => STOP and ASK.

components.summary: A colour picker: a swatch trigger opening a colour canvas + a 16-colour preset palette (color-picker.vue). Supports transparent. For branding/widget/threshold/severity colours.
The grid/table dropdown (obs-grid-select) — a dropdown whose menu is a searchable TABLE (columns, checkboxes, sort, badge, View/Clear Selected, rich cells). The Select Agent/Monitor picker (~70×).
The DS metric/KPI list (obs-metric-list) — a prominent value + unit + label per row (dashboard KPI widgets). Split from the Table vertical-value variant.
The DS key-value / description list (obs-key-value) — a tinted label cell + value per row (a record detail view). Split from the Table key-value variant.

The list/detail PAGE HEADER at the top of a page: an optional back button OR a section menu-toggle + the title (--primary-alt, weight 500, 18px) + an optional count pill on the left, and right-side actions (search / export / primary Add) via the default slot, over a --border-color bottom rule. Split from the product’s Toolbars family. Feature-complete variants: default · with-count · back · menu-toggle (module SECTION header, shows/hides obs-side-menu) · with-subtitle · with-breadcrumb · detail-meta (RUM/APM span-detail strip) · monitor-detail · title-only · no-divider. NOT the strip above a list/table (that is obs-toolbar), NOT between-page navigation (obs-sidebar / obs-breadcrumbs), and NOT the global app top-bar (obs-app-header).
components.selectHint: Title + primary actions at the TOP of a page (list or detail)? -> obs-page-header.

components.summary: The GLOBAL top bar present on every authenticated page: the brand/logo on the left, and on the right a row of circular action icon-buttons (global search / health monitoring / approval / notifications with a count badge), a BUILD version tag, and the user avatar/menu. App CHROME — a SEPARATE archetype from obs-page-header (the per-page title bar); it pairs with obs-sidebar (the left module nav). Bar: 50px tall, --page-background-color, a --border-color bottom rule. Circular buttons 36×36 (--neutral-light; --primary when the route is active); notification badge --secondary-red; avatar --primary.
components.selectHint: The GLOBAL bar at the very top of every page (logo + global search + notifications + user)? -> obs-app-header.

components.summary: The interactive header ACCOUNT menu — an avatar/initials trigger that opens a dropdown with a user header, account links, an optional theme toggle, and a danger Logout. Self-contained (renders its own trigger + top-layer popover) so it drops into obs-app-header's `user` slot, or stands alone. The turnkey form of the `user-menu` recipe.
components.selectHint: The header avatar + account dropdown (My Profile / Setup / Docs / theme / Logout)? -> obs-user-menu in the app-header `user` slot. For a generic action menu use obs-menu; for nav use obs-sidebar/obs-side-menu.

components.summary: The interactive header NOTIFICATION panel — a bell + unread-count badge trigger that opens a dropdown with a title, Alerts/System tabs, a scrollable list of notification rows (severity dot + text + time), and a View all / Clear all footer. Self-contained (renders its own trigger + top-layer popover) so it drops into obs-app-header, or stands alone. The turnkey form of the `notification-dropdown` recipe.
components.selectHint: The header bell + notification panel (alerts/system, badge count)? -> obs-notification-menu in the app-header action area. For a generic action menu use obs-menu; the account dropdown is obs-user-menu.

components.summary: The interactive header GLOBAL SEARCH / omnibox — a single search bar with a leading category picker, a query field, and an Execute action (+ a parse-error state + clear). For cross-app search / a command surface, NOT a plain list filter. Composes obs-select (category) + obs-input (query) + obs-icon. The turnkey form of the `command-palette` recipe.
components.selectHint: A GLOBAL / cross-app search or command surface (category + query + Execute) in the header? -> obs-command-palette. A plain search of a single list/table? -> the obs-input `search` type, NOT this.

components.summary: The control strip that frames a LIST/TABLE or a widget. Three compositions via `variant`: grid (default) — a strip ABOVE a grid with search (start slot) on the left and filter / column-chooser / primary Add (default slot) on the right; bulk — the floating SELECTION pill (a clear checkbox + "N items selected" + a divider + the bulk actions), shown once rows are selected, emits `clear`; widget — a widget header (title + a time-range pill + a kebab of actions) with rounded-top chrome. NOT the page title bar (obs-page-header) and NOT the global top bar (obs-app-header). Compose the contents from DS elements (obs-input, obs-button, obs-checkbox, obs-icon, obs-select).
components.selectHint: A search / filter / column / Add strip ABOVE a list or table? -> obs-toolbar (variant=grid, the default).

components.summary: The product's PRIMARY navigation — the left vertical MODULE rail (FlotoNavBar). Collapsed to 65px (brand mark + module icons) by default; HOVER-expands to 170px (ObserveOps wordmark + labels), or pin it open with `expanded`. Data-driven module list (icon + label, optional BETA tag); the active module highlights --primary on --nav-panel-bg, a hovered non-active item gets a --nav-hover-bg pill. Theme-aware. Pairs with obs-app-header (the horizontal top bar). NOT an in-module section menu (side-menu) and NOT sibling-view switching (obs-tabs).
components.selectHint: Switch between top-level product MODULES (Dashboards / Monitors / Alerts / …)? -> obs-sidebar (the left module rail).

components.summary: The location TRAIL (+ an optional back chevron): a path of crumbs (Reports / Compliance / PCI-DSS Audit) with the current (last) crumb in weight 500 and the ancestors as muted links. Shows where the user is and gives a one-click way up one or many levels. Data-driven `items`; separator is `/` (default) or a chevron. Lives in a page header (obs-page-header has a `breadcrumb` slot). NOT module switching (obs-sidebar), NOT sibling views (obs-tabs), NOT a graph-expansion trail.
components.selectHint: Show the user's LOCATION plus a way up one or MANY levels? -> obs-breadcrumbs (the trail).

components.summary: The in-module SECTION navigation panel — a searchable, collapsible left menu. ONE element with a `mode` axis folding the product's five side-menu forms: settings (THE Settings menu — left-menu.vue: a MULTI-OPEN collapse with the expand chevron on the RIGHT, full-width dividers between sections, and children as an indented ROUNDED-highlight menu), sections (a leaner accordion form — LEFT chevron + an inset --primary left-rule active), categories (dashboard picker, count tags), tree (Log/Topology N-level hierarchy with type icon + count badge), and list (report/saved-views flat list, optional ★ favourite). Data-driven via a recursive `items` model; optional top segmented `tabs` + a search box. NOT the module rail (obs-sidebar), NOT sibling views (obs-tabs), NOT the faceted checkbox filter (a vertical Filter). SIZING: the element is width:100% (fills its container) — set the container WIDTH per mode (settings|sections ~15% / categories ~30vw / tree|list ~20%); see `sizing` + usageRules[mode].width. The element OWNS its own chrome — a flush white panel with a RIGHT border/divider, its own internal padding, and an automatic TOP/BOTTOM scroll FADE (content dissolves into the panel at whichever edge can still scroll) — so the host column adds NEITHER a border NOR padding (they would double up).
components.selectHint: The in-module SECTION / category navigation panel — a left menu / left nav for a module (settings menu, category list, saved-views list, sections/tree). NOT the module rail (obs-sidebar) and NOT sibling views (obs-tabs).

components.summary: Renders a product monitor-type LOGO by name (Router, Linux, Windows, MySQL, Docker, AWS, …) — the full-colour brand/technology marks from the product logo library (Assets → Logos). The logo counterpart of obs-icon: use a LOGO for a technology / vendor / monitor-type (they carry brand colour); use an ICON for a UI affordance (monochrome, inherits text colour). Names are case/space-insensitive and alias-friendly (docker → dockercontainer, aws → aws-cloud, vmware → vmware-esxi); an unknown name falls back to the generic `no-icon`. A CURATED common set (~114) is bundled; the full 242 live on the Assets → Logos page.
components.selectHint: A technology / vendor / monitor-type mark that carries BRAND COLOUR (Linux, Docker, AWS, MySQL)? -> obs-logo.

components.summary: The two-part METRIC selection panel — a 'Select Monitor' dropdown on top (reuses obs-select) + a searchable, grouped metric/counter TREE below (categories → counters, each optionally with a unit/instances). It LOOKS like a side menu (a hierarchical tree), but its job is selecting a VALUE (a counter to plot/query), not navigation — so it lives with the Form Controls, as a turnkey preset over obs-select's tree-select. Data-driven: give it `monitors` + a `metrics` tree; it emits `select-monitor` and `select`. Source-derived from metric-explorer/metric-picker.vue (MonitorPicker + CounterSelector).
components.selectHint: Selecting a METRIC/counter (monitor → grouped, searchable counter tree) to plot or query? -> obs-metric-picker. A generic dropdown -> obs-select. NAVIGATING sections -> obs-side-menu (it looks similar but navigates; this selects a value).

components.summary: The NOC / wallboard ROTATOR chrome — a top bar that auto-cycles a set of dashboards on a countdown: logo (left) · ‹ prev · current title · next › (center) · countdown + play/pause + exit (right), over a body slot that holds the current dashboard. Self-contained playback: an internal countdown timer auto-advances; ← / → step, space pauses, Esc exits. Data-agnostic: it owns the rotation and emits `change`/`close`; the consumer renders the actual dashboard (a widget grid — a data-viz gap) in the default slot. Part of the Playback & Timeline family. Source-derived from dashboard/noc-player.vue.
components.selectHint: A full-screen wallboard that rotates DASHBOARDS on a timer (NOC mode)? -> obs-noc-player. To step a time WINDOW under a chart -> obs-timeline-scrollbar. The normal app top bar -> obs-app-header.

components.summary: The temporal NAVIGATOR bar — batch (« ») and single-step (‹ ›) controls around a START–END time WINDOW of bucketed snapshots. Left: batch-back + step-back + the window start; right: the window end + step-forward + batch-forward. Data/behaviour-agnostic: it renders the controls + times and emits `shift {direction, batch}`; the consumer moves its data window. Part of the Playback & Timeline family. Source-derived from netroute/timeline-scrollbar.vue.
components.selectHint: A stepper to move a TIME WINDOW back/forward over bucketed snapshots (netroute history / a temporal chart)? -> obs-timeline-scrollbar. To PICK an absolute date/range -> obs-date-time-picker. To rotate DASHBOARDS -> obs-noc-player.

components.summary: An inline notice / callout — a tinted surface with a status icon and a message. Intents: info (default), success, warning, error.
components.selectHint: A persistent inline message tied to a section (form hint, visibility notice). For transient feedback use a toast; for a blocking decision use obs-modal.

components.summary: The reusable icon element (<obs-icon>) — renders a real product glyph from the shared library (_icons.js, extracted from src/assets/icons/icons.js; ~548 glyphs) by `name`. Accepts kebab (chevron-double-left) or camelCase (chevronDoubleLeft). Reactive: change `name` and the glyph swaps. Inherits the surrounding text color (currentColor) and takes a px/CSS-length `size`. Renders per-icon fill-rule/clip-rule, so glyphs with holes/overlaps (e.g. the theme-auto half-circle) draw correctly. Decorative by default; pass `label` for an accessible name. This is how any icon should be used across the DS — never hand-drawn/inlined SVG.
components.selectHint: Any GLYPH (search, chevron, status/action icon)? -> obs-icon name="…". A brand / monitor-type LOGO (Motadata, Citrix, Router, Kubernetes…)? -> obs-logo, NOT obs-icon. A coloured severity dot? -> obs-severity.

components.summary: Teal key:value pills for a current selection inside a picker/multi-select trigger. Truncates to max-items, then a "+N" pill opens a popover listing the rest. Display-only (the home of the teal pills, read-only mode).

A single ring gauge — the product's Monitor-Availability / Alert-Count dial. A track ring with a severity-coloured arc swept to value/total, a large mono number in the centre, and an optional label beneath. The DS chart library flags "gauge" as a CUSTOM-ENGINE type (data-only, no serializable config); this element IS that renderer, as a drop-in web component.
components.selectHint: Use for a single count-against-a-total dial coloured by a severity/status level (Up, Down, Critical, Warning…). One gauge = one slice of a group; lay several in a row to show a whole group (Monitor Availability, Alert Count). Not for a trend over time (use a line/area chart) and not for a share-of-total breakdown as one figure (use a donut/pie).

components.summary: The product's Infrastructure-Heatmap honeycomb (PlainHeatMap) — one hexagon per monitor, each filled with its severity colour, packed into a honeycomb grid. Hovering a hex raises the product tooltip (monitor name/IP + location + a severity pill). The DS chart library flags "heat-map" as a CUSTOM-ENGINE type (data-only, no serializable renderer); this element IS that renderer, ported 1:1 from the product's heatmap-single-group.vue — a border-coloured hex box with a 1px-inset severity cell (the thin outline), size x 1.1547 height and a size x 0.2885 honeycomb pull-up.
components.selectHint: Use to show the health of MANY monitors at a glance as a dense honeycomb coloured by severity — the Infrastructure Heatmap on a dashboard. One hex = one monitor. Not for a small set with per-row detail (use a table), not for a single value against a total (use a gauge), and not for a trend over time (use a line/area chart).

components.summary: The dashboard widget CHROME: a framed card with a grey header (title + a hover-revealed time badge + a hover-revealed kebab menu of Full Screen / Share / Edit / Clone / Remove), a body slot for any widget content (chart, gauge, heatmap, table…), the header as a drag handle, and a bottom-right resize grip. The card does not own its position — it emits card-dragstart / card-resizestart (composed, bubbling) so an obs-widget-grid parent can drive the layout, plus an action event for the kebab items.
components.selectHint: Use to wrap ONE widget on a dashboard grid — it is the frame around a chart/gauge/heatmap, not the chart itself. Inside a grid it becomes draggable (by its header) and resizable (bottom-right grip). Need a plain content card that is NOT a dashboard widget (a settings panel, a summary tile, a form card)? -> use a generic card, not obs-widget-card. Put the visualization in the default slot; don't reach for the chart element directly on the board.

components.summary: A live draggable / droppable / resizable dashboard grid — the framework-agnostic answer to vue-grid-layout. Slot in obs-widget-card children carrying data-x/data-y/data-w/data-h; the grid snaps each to a 12-column layout, pushes colliding cards down, compacts everything up under gravity, and auto-scrolls the page while you drag or resize a card past the fold. Emits layout-change with the settled positions.
components.selectHint: Reach for this when a user must arrange their OWN dashboard — drag cards around, resize them, and have the layout persist. If the layout is fixed and authored by you (never rearranged at runtime), use a plain CSS grid instead — this element carries drag/resize/collision machinery you don't need.
